options.why: Your special conversion is by day, so a nonbook night can have no ordinary visit like Oracle’s astral action.
options.exposure: No Aegis exists. A later book attack or a surviving hit from your pre-conversion defense can draw scrutiny.
options.bestWhen: You preserve the conversion and are not performing direct book attacks.
strategy: Write a Town role choice for Aegis, not the numbered player you might later Indoctrinate.
Alternate role choices and use Oracle itself only once. A quiet night does not independently support a save.
Keep the recruit’s role and changed faction private; Oracle does not reveal exact identities or conversions.
Reassess the no-visit history before taking book duty. Your Basic Defense before conversion is a separate real ability, not proof Aegis protected you.

options.why: A book attack can share one claimed Barrier destination on an actual direct-visit night.
options.exposure: Neither conversion nor the book grants Barrier. Nonbook idle nights lack normal Cleric visits.
options.bestWhen: You expect to carry the book and have a compatible direct-visit history.
strategy: Use the actual night book destination as the claimed Barrier target, not the player selected for a daytime conversion.
Answer TP and keep quiet target bookkeeping without inventing saved feedback.
Do not leak the new Coven member’s retained Town ability as though Cleric mechanically learned their role.
After successful Indoctrinate you lose your initial Basic Defense. Do not imply this is a permanent Cleric protection state or unlimited self-Barrier.

options.why: Before conversion your Basic Defense can resemble one limited Bodyguard Self Protect survival, and a book visit can share a Guard destination.
options.exposure: Your defense is not a Bodyguard counterattack or Guard interception. Repeated self-shields and promised protection can be disproved.
options.bestWhen: A specific early survived Basic attack or a direct book route makes the limited resemblance relevant.
strategy: If explaining an early survived Basic hit as Self Protect, keep the Bodyguard two-use limit; Cultist’s pre-conversion defense is not an unlimited shield story.
A self-shield night does not also Guard another player, and a direct book visit is a separate actual action.
Do not invent a successful counterattack or saved resident. Cultist does not cancel an enemy visitor’s action as Guard would.
After conversion your Basic Defense disappears. Plan around the real loss and do not claim the retained defense proves Town.

options.why: A direct book target can fit a single Sheriff check, with private team information sometimes guiding discussion.
options.exposure: Cultist provides no night suspicion result, and idle nights or daytime conversion do not create a check visit.
options.bestWhen: You are making real direct book visits and accept a more demanding early report history.
strategy: Use the actual book destination as the checked player; a daytime recruit is not a night-visited Sheriff target.
Post early with Innocent or Suspicious, keeping exact private recruit or role knowledge out of the result.
Remember that a converted Town role changes faction but retains its role. Do not assume old public role confirmation means current Town faction.
Do not write a completed check on a genuinely idle nonbook night. This is a route-dependent fallback, not evidence supplied by conversion.

options.why: A nonbook night with no action resembles Deputy’s night inactivity.
options.exposure: You cannot produce a day shot, and conversion is not a Deputy demonstration. Your Basic Defense can also complicate a casual story.
options.bestWhen: You accept demonstration pressure and want a sparse inactive-night account.
strategy: Keep the public history about a day resource rather than invented nightly investigation results.
Do not present Indoctrinate as a shot or imply the recruit’s changed faction is visible Deputy confirmation.
Deputy has one real charge; an alleged miss is not independent proof and cannot be repeated as an unlimited excuse.
If the book is passed to you, its direct visit no longer fits a completely inactive night story. Reassess before making that switch.

options.why: A direct book destination can be the selected member in a normal one-target Psychic vision.
options.exposure: No genuine group is supplied, and genuinely idle nonbook nights have the wrong movement footprint.
options.bestWhen: You take book duty and want day group influence despite significant ongoing maintenance.
strategy: Include the actual direct night destination as the selected member, not the person converted during the day.
Keep N1 Good pairs and N2 Evil trios and post near day start.
A recruit retaining a confirmed Town role can now have Coven faction; do not confuse role identity with apparent faction when reasoning about group constraints.
Keep conversion and exact-role team knowledge private. Psychic does not announce a complete roster, and a valid-looking invented group does not supply protection or proof.
